# 0063 — Why the Beta Readers Missed Chapter 5 Scene Compression & Assumed Chat Context (`Law 13: Cold-Reader Zero-Assumed-Context, Named-Extra Economy & Anti-Compression Gate`) (`2026-10-22`)

## Plain-English Summary
When John began editing `CHAPTERS-01-TO-05-MANUSCRIPT-v8.docx` (`CHAPTERS-01-TO-05-MANUSCRIPT-v8 - jcl edits.docx`), he stopped at Chapter 5 (`P1261–P1263`, corresponding to `L2523–L2527`) because the Friday lunch GHH audition continuation in the Pit and the surrounding October transitions were severely over-compressed (`254w`, `387w`, and `295w` mega-paragraphs with multiple speakers in a single paragraph) and assumed background knowledge from the author/steward planning chat rather than staging the scene for a first-time reader. Furthermore, the draft invented an unnecessary named minor character (`"Evan Liu"`) when none of the other audition applicants in Chapter 3 had names and when the **two smiley pizza-hack boys from Chapter 3** (who were accepted into GHH in Chapter 3) were already established in canon to carry those beats.

## Root-Cause Diagnosis: Why Did the 6-Seat Beta-Reader Panel Miss This?
1. **Failure Mode 1 — Shared-Context Blindness in Seat 1 (`First-Time Cold Reader`):**
   - Seat 1 was checking whether plot beats from the brief were *present* (`"spark jump"`, `"moved four envoy pieces at once"`, `"Dr. Lin's classroom puzzle"`), rather than simulating a reader with **zero access to the planning chat** who only knows what was on the page in Chapters 1–4.
   - As a result, Seat 1 failed to ask:
     - *Why are GHH auditions continuing on Friday at lunch?* (Because the *Grand Street Pizza* frenzy in Chapter 3 cut off tryouts before the last four names on Zara's list got a turn, and Julian was out of school Wednesday and Thursday upstate at Halcyon.)
     - *What is on the Pit's big projection screen and how is Julian controlling it?* (Writing `"while he moved four envoy pieces at once without touching his mouse"` as a 10-word clause without first staging the nervous applicant's *AtlasCraft* bridge trial, showing that four GHH defender envoys normally take Noah and Priya two keyboards to steer, and showing Julian's hands resting flat on the desk in plain view while his glasses spark and the four envoys + terminal windows move by themselves left the reader guessing what was even on screen.)
2. **Failure Mode 2 — The Frozen Paragraph-Count Compression Trap (`1,398` Paragraphs) in Seat 5 (`Line & Structural Editor`):**
   - Previously, `check_v8.py` compared `v8_rej == base_acc` without filtering empty strings from inserted `<w:p>` elements (`[x for x in lst if x]`). To avoid changing the total paragraph count (`1,398`), four distinct scenes in Chapter 5 were crammed into three giant existing paragraph slots (`P1261` at `254` words, `P1262` at `387` words, and `P1263` at `295` words containing `5` separate dialogue quotes from `3` different speakers!).
   - Seat 5 checked semicolons and em-dashes, but had no gate prohibiting **multi-speaker paragraphs**, **mega-paragraphs (`> 175` words)**, or **telegraphed scene compression**.
3. **Failure Mode 3 — Missing Named-Extra Economy & Callback Reuse Gate in Seat 3 (`Continuity & World-Rules Auditor`):**
   - In Chapter 3, none of the GHH applicants had names—they were memorable by their *actions* (the Captain Hook boy, **the two pizza-hack boys**, and **the boy whose avatar Julian aged into a 76-year-old grandpa**). Inventing a brand-new named character (`"Evan Liu"`) in Chapter 5 forced the reader to ask *"Who is Evan, why does he have a name when no one else did, and why is he recording things?"* when the **two smiley GHH pizza-hack boys** (wearing their new black GHH lanyards up front in the Pit and bragging in the Friday cafeteria lunch line) and the **grandpa-avatar boy** (leading Monday's cafeteria toast in Chapter 7) were sitting right there in Chapter 3 canon.

## Permanent Fixes Applied to Chekhov (`Law 13`)
1. **Seat 1 (`First-Time Cold Reader`) — Zero-Assumed-Context & Stage-Setting Gate:**
   - Seat 1 must evaluate every scene transition and visual payoff assuming **zero knowledge of the planning chat**. Every scene must explicitly establish: (a) *Why Here / Why Now* on the page, (b) *Room & Screen Geometry* before the visual payoff fires, and (c) *Visible Cause-and-Effect* (`ct` commentating from the server rack, Julian's hands flat on the desk, the blue-white spark jumping from his glasses to his temple, the four envoys moving by themselves on the eighty-inch projection screen, and kids in the benches whispering about the spark).
2. **Seat 3 (`Continuity & World-Rules Auditor`) — Named-Extra Economy & Canon Callback Rule:**
   - Flag as a **BLOCKER** any newly invented first-and-last-name minor character introduced to carry exposition when an established canon character or memorable unnamed callback from an earlier chapter (such as the **two smiley GHH pizza-hack boys from Chapter 3** in their new club lanyards) can fulfill the role organically. Also verify zero occurrences of common name typos (`Crovo` -> `Corvo`) or forbidden architectural jargon (`lintel`, `parapet`, `lancet`, `filigree`).
3. **Seat 5 (`Line & Structural Editor`) & `check_*.py` — No-Mega-Paragraph & One-Speaker-Per-Paragraph Gate:**
   - Every deterministic chapter check (`check_v8.py`, `check_ch678_manuscript_v2.py`) now enforces:
     - **Zero paragraphs `> 175` words** in any revised/drafted chapter.
     - **One speaker per paragraph** (never combine dialogue from two or more characters inside a single paragraph).
     - **Non-empty paragraph list comparison (`[x for x in v8_rej if x] == [x for x in base_acc if x]`)** in `docx-redline` roundtrip checks so adding proper paragraph breaks in revised chapters is never penalized by a frozen paragraph count.
